newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sacked Indonesia MP to be questioned over cards.
newsitem.headline: Sacked Indonesia MP to be questioned over cards.

text.p: Sacked Indonesian legislator Sri Bintang Pamungkas is to be questioned over festive cards he sent urging people to boycott the May 29 general elections, authorities said on Wednesday.

Inside the cards, sent to mark last month's Moslem festival of Eid al-Fitr, Bintang also enclosed the programmes of the party he set up last year, the unrecognised United Democratic Party of Indonesia (PUDI), regarding the general elections.
"We will question him," Attorney-General Singgih told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
Singgih did not elaborate, but said the authorities would take the same measures as they did for other people who breached the law.
The PUDI urged Indonesians to boycott the general elections and reject possible re-election of President Suharto in presidential polls next year.
The High Court last month upheld a lower court decision to sentence Bintang to 34 months in jail for defaming Suharto during a speech he made to Indonesian students in Berlin in April 1995.
But Bintang is still free pending a final order to be jailed. He was not immediately available for comment on the cards, a copy of which was received by Reuters.
Bintang was sacked by the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) in 1995 for being too outspoken.

Media Indonesia newspaper reported on Wednesday that the military has seized at least 6,000 pamphlets asking Indonesians to boycott the elections and is searching for those responsible for producing the material.

The newspaper quoted Major-General Tayo Tarmadi, head of the Siliwangi military command which oversees West Java province, as saying on Tuesday that the pamphlets had been found at a boarding house in Bandung, the capital of West Java.

Only three political parties are allowed to put up candidates for elections in Indonesia and some voters stay away from polling in protest. The government has banned any encouragement for people not to vote.
